$comment: Baseline of tests that are CURRENTLY FAILING because they have found a real
defect that has not been fixed yet. `npm run test:all` compares each run
- a failure listed here        -> reported as KNOWN, does not fail the run
- a failure NOT listed here    -> reported as NEW REGRESSION, fails the run
- a listed test that now PASSES -> reported as FIXED; delete its entry
This keeps the suite usable as a merge gate while the documented defects are
still open, without ever hiding them. Every entry must name the defect and
where the fix belongs — an entry with no `fix` is not allowed to be added.
Match is on the test's full name (suite path + test title), substring-matched.
See docs/TESTING.md for the full triage writeup.

issues.title: division_title_prob / first_round_bye_prob / conf_champ_prob / super_bowl_prob are scaled from playoff_prob by magic multipliers instead of being simulated, so mutually exclusive outcomes do not sum to 1
issues.fix: tools/export_web_datasets.R lines ~147 and ~176: replace `playoff_prob * 0.62`, the 0.65/0.08 bye split and the 0.02/0.05 fallbacks with values read from the playoff simulator, then renormalise per division/conference.
tests: exactly one team wins each division
exactly one team per conference gets the first-round bye
exactly one team per conference wins the conference
exactly one team wins the Super Bowl

issues.title: 36 of 91 graded games present a projected margin that contradicts their own correct/incorrect badge; the badges imply 61.5% accuracy while the displayed margins imply 50.5%
issues.fix: tools/export_web_datasets.R ~line 265: `h_win_prob` is chosen by comparing `pred_winner == h_name` against the accuracy-history record, then `projected_margin` is reconstructed from it via qnorm. Make the export carry the originally predicted margin instead of reconstructing it, or fix the name comparison.
tests: prediction_correct agrees with the projected margin and the result
no completed card pairs a correct projection with an Upset badge

issues.title: The /diagnostics calibration curve is a hardcoded literal, not computed from graded predictions: its bin counts total all 272 scheduled games while only 92 have been played
issues.fix: tools/export_web_datasets.R lines 614-625: compute calibration_curve by binning the model's actual graded predictions instead of writing a literal list.
tests: calibration bin counts sum to the number of games actually graded

issues.fix: app/layout.tsx: offset the content column by the sidebar width (e.g. `lg:pl-64` on the flex-1 wrapper), or let the sidebar participate in the flex flow instead of being `fixed`.

issues.title: PlayersClient never resets currentPage when the search or team filter changes, so filtering from page 2+ renders an empty table while the footer still reports matches
issues.fix: components/PlayersClient.tsx: add `useEffect(() => setCurrentPage(1), [searchQuery, selectedTeam])`, or clamp currentPage to totalPages.

issues.title: Margin sigma is hardcoded in three separate components with two different values: Sidebar.tsx says 14.6 (correct) while app/page.tsx says 13.8 and PlayoffBracketSimulator.tsx simulates with 13.8. The sidebar and the home-page banner contradict each other on screen.
issues.fix: Read margin_sigma and home_field_adv from model_diagnostics.json in all three places. app/page.tsx: pass the diagnostics dataset into the sigma chip. components/Sidebar.tsx: it hardcodes 14.6 four times (lines ~207, 217, 220, 221) and takes no props, so it needs the value threading through or a shared constants module. components/PlayoffBracketSimulator.tsx: accept sigma/HFA as props instead of inlining 13.8 and 1.8. This is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md records as WNBA Finding C-1.
tests: the home page sigma chip matches model_diagnostics.margin_sigma
PlayoffBracketSimulator simulates with the real sigma, not a literal
PlayoffBracketSimulator uses the real home-field advantage
all hardcoded margin sigma literals agree with each other

issues.title: Once the mobile nav drawer is open it paints over its own close button, and the drawer has no close control of its own, so the backdrop is the only way out
